origin.description: Return the 1-based indices of string where there is at least one match to pattern. This is which(str_detect(string, pattern)), and the same positions as grep.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares bytes, and coll uses the locale's collation rules. The empty string and boundary patterns are not allowed.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, return the indices that do not match. Must be a single TRUE or FALSE.

origin.details: A missing detection is not a match, so a missing string is never an index. When pattern is longer than a length-1 string, the indices refer to that longer detection vector. Names of the true elements are kept when detection kept names. No matches on a named result is a named empty integer vector.
origin.value: An integer vector, usually shorter than string.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_which(fruit, "a")
writeLines(paste0('str_which(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "a") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Return the 1-based indices where str_detect is true.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Passed to str_detect. A plain string is a regular expression. fixed, coll, and regex select that engine.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, return the indices that do not match.

translation.details: Only values that are True are kept. NA is not an index. The index is the position in the detection vector, which can be longer than string when a length-1 string is paired with a longer pattern. Names follow the detection result.
translation.value: A list of ints. No matches is an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringr.detect import str_which
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_which(fruit, "a")
print('str_which(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "a") returns ' + ", ".join(str(item) for item in result) + '.')
